manifest.provenance: Exact 600-page PDF acquired over HTTPS from the Internet Archive item OLM1981. The scanned title page and decree identify the 1981 second typical edition; the file carries an Adobe Paper Capture optical text layer over page images.
manifest.notes: Artifact page numbers and the book's Roman-numeral Praenotanda pagination coincide for the front matter: artifact page 32 is printed page XXXII. Every registered passage records artifact pages. The optical text layer is a discovery aid only; the registered passages were read in rendered page images at 200 dpi. Only those pages were inspected.

manifest.rights_basis: MIXED, WHICH IS WHY THESE EXACT WHOLE-BOOK BYTES ARE NOT TRACKED OR REDISTRIBUTED. The underlying English of the 1937 and 1945 registered editions is in the United States public domain by failure to renew, established at registration-number level in src/sources/inventories/lasance-new-roman-missal-rights-v1.toml. This later printing also contains the appendix at printed pages 1298a-1298n, new matter first published after October 1954 for which that record establishes no registration, renewal result, or publication date from a physical copy. Other lettered insert matter, including printed pages 1302a-1302d, has likewise not been established as part of either registered edition. A single rights status cannot say public domain except for unresolved leaves, so this record is unresolved over the whole PDF. The independently registered tracked OCR derivative artifact.francis-xavier-lasance.the-new-roman-missal.benziger-revised-1945.new-roman-missal-text-80b34759 excludes pages 1298a-1298n and 1302a-1302d and carries the affirmative United States public-domain basis used for publication. The page images registered here are evidence for visual inspection and exact loci, not a redistribution source. Nothing rests on availability from, or any rights representation by, the Internet Archive.
manifest.provenance: Fetched as the complete PDF with curl from the exact URL above on 2026-08-26 into the repository's ignored .scratch area and hashed before use. The complete object is 75,268,976 bytes and 1,879 PDF pages. PDF metadata identifies an Adobe Acrobat 8.1 combined full-page facsimile created and modified on 2009-07-07; those technical dates do not identify the book's edition or printing. Internet Archive's whole scandata XML was separately fetched from https://archive.org/download/fr-lasance-missal-1937/fr-lasance-missal-1937_scandata.xml for the leaf-to-printed-page audit: 668,982 bytes, sha256 217d6b70f6645fe88b7b6028983297a4c84200ea079d2434c881b7310fb1212e. Every registered prayer page was rendered from these exact PDF bytes and visually inspected. No model stood between either server response and its recorded hash or size, or between the PDF and its recorded page count.
manifest.notes: Internet Archive item fr-lasance-missal-1937 is an opaque delivery locator supplied by a private uploader, not bibliographic evidence. Its name is wrong: the exact images show the Benziger 1945 revised edition in a printing of about 1955-56, as established and bounded in the edition record and the Lasance rights inventory. Do not describe this artifact as the 1937 edition or broaden it into a witness for a different edition. Artifact page N corresponds to Internet Archive BookReader leaf n(N-1); the passage records state the visible printed pagination, full IA leaf range, and full one-based artifact-page range independently. Every page image is stamped http://ccwatershed.org, but no host rights claim is relied on. Exact wording was read from rendered page images; the OCR artifacts remain finding aids only.

manifest.rights_basis: The identified printed book was published by Friedrich Pustet in 1888. Its 1888 printed contents have no remaining United States copyright term in 2026: a 95-year maximum term ended before 2026, and any URAA restoration supplies only the remainder of the otherwise applicable United States term. Faithful mechanical scans and project transcription of those public-domain words add no human authorship. The stated basis is publication date and mechanical reproduction, not Internet Archive availability or a host label.
